sculpture.name: statyett, Kvinnofigur, figurine
sculpture.title: statyett, Kvinnofigur, figurine
sculpture.reason: A seated wooden female figure with scarification marks, a stylized bird-head hairstyle, and carved integral stool — a classic Senufo pombibele/tugubele type ancestor/diviner figure, consistent with Senufo sculptural tradition from Mali.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A standing wooden female figure with hands on hips, conical coiffure/headdress, and classic Senufo facial styling (closed eyes, elongated nose) — a well-known Senufo sculptural type, consistent with the museum's attribution.

sculpture.name: Sculpture
sculpture.title: Nursing Woman with Child
sculpture.reason: A wooden seated maternity (nursing mother) figure with the elongated face, pursed lips, and scarification typical of Senufo carving from the Korhogo region of Côte d'Ivoire — a classic Senufo sculptural genre.

sculpture.name: Träskulptur, statyett, figurine
sculpture.title: Träskulptur, statyett, figurine
sculpture.reason: The carving shows a seated female figure supporting a lidded vessel ("medicine chest" with bird-form lid) on her head, a well-documented Senufo sculptural type (cf. Kjersmeier reference), matching the claimed ethnicity and origin (Ivory Coast).

sculpture.name: statyett, Trästatyett, figurine
sculpture.title: statyett, Trästatyett, figurine
sculpture.reason: A wooden figure of a seated woman on a stool with scarification marks and a bowl/animal-figure headdress, collected in Ivory Coast and attributed to the Senufo people — a classic Senufo pombibele/maternity-type figure form.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: Carved wooden standing female figure with scarification patterns, hands on hips, elongated form — a classic Senufo rhythm-pounder/ancestor figure type, consistent with the museum's attribution.

sculpture.name: statyett, Trästatyett, figurine
sculpture.title: statyett, Trästatyett, figurine
sculpture.reason: The image shows a tall wooden standing figure with elongated body, bird/animal figure atop the coiffure, and geometric facial features — a classic Senufo rhythm-pounder/ancestor-type figure style, consistent with the museum's Senufo attribution.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden male standing figure with cap, bearded face, incised facial marks, and hands at waist—consistent with Senufo ancestor/memorial figure sculpture traditions.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: Carved wood face mask with horns, geometric cheek designs, and dangling leg-like elements is a classic Senufo-type wooden mask form used in ritual/masquerade contexts, consistent with the claimed attribution.

masks-ritual.name: sculpture
masks-ritual.title: sculpture
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden head with pointed cap and flanking projections, museum attributes it to Senufo production—consistent with Senufo carving traditions of Mali/Côte d'Ivoire; plausible as a helmet-mask or figure fragment used ritually.

masks-ritual.name: stav, Dansstav, staff
masks-ritual.title: stav, Dansstav, staff
masks-ritual.reason: This is a wooden dance staff with a carved zoomorphic (bird/animal) head finial, collected among the Senufo in Mali and matching known Senufo "crosse de voleur rituel" type dance staffs used in ritual/ceremonial contexts. It is a carved wooden implement rather than a true weapon, but fits the Senufo material culture.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden face mask with tall curved horn-like crest and tusks, consistent with Senufo kpelie/related mask traditions from Mali/Côte d'Ivoire; museum attributes it to Senufo makers.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: This is a carved wooden helmet mask in the form of an animal head (elongated jaw with teeth, pointed ears) with a worn, blackened-brown patina, consistent with Senufo zoomorphic ritual masks (e.g., firespitter/kponyugu type) used in initiation and funerary contexts.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden mask with horned crest, black and red staining, and stylized facial features typical of Senufo mask-making traditions (Poro society masks); this style is well documented among the Senufo of Mali/Côte d'Ivoire.

masks-ritual.name: dance-mask
masks-ritual.title: dance-mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden zoomorphic helmet mask with antelope-like horns, tusks, and open-mouthed muzzle, a classic form of Senufo "firespitter" (wanyugo) style dance masks used in ritual/initiation contexts. This matches known Senufo mask production well.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: The mask shows a stylized human face with horns, carved ridges, and dangling earrings, a wooden ritual mask type well documented among the Senufo of Mali/Côte d'Ivoire, matching the museum's attribution.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden zoomorphic dance mask with buffalo-like horns, characteristic of Senufo ritual mask traditions from Mali/Côte d'Ivoire; fits the claimed culture and category well.

masks-ritual.name: dance-mask
masks-ritual.title: dance-mask
masks-ritual.reason: A wooden zoomorphic mask combining hyena-like features, antelope horns, and a bird atop the forehead — this composite animal mask form is characteristic of Senufo ritual/initiation masks (Poro society). Consistent with the claimed maker.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A patched brown cotton hide-like mask with cowrie-shell-edged eyeholes, fur trim, and bone/leather toggles — this matches the known Senufo type of textile "bogolan"-style ritual mask worn in Poro society ceremonies, plausible for Mali.

masks-ritual.name: dance-mask
masks-ritual.title: dance-mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden dance mask with animal (baboon-like) features and traditional red/white pigmentation, consistent with Senufo ritual mask traditions; museum attributes it to Senufo.

instruments.name: drum
instruments.title: drum
instruments.reason: A large wooden slit/membrane drum carved in relief with a mask face, animals, and standing figures, mounted on four legs — a classic Senufo carved wooden drum form, consistent with known Senufo ceremonial drums.

instruments.name: musical horn
instruments.title: musical horn
instruments.reason: A composite antelope-horn instrument covered in fur/skin with a carrying cord, a signal/musical horn consistent with Senufo craft traditions of Mali/Côte d'Ivoire region; museum credits Senufo makers.

instruments.name: trumma
instruments.title: trumma
instruments.reason: A standing wooden slit/membrane drum carved in relief with figures (woman, snakes, turtle, lizard), standing on four feet with a skin head tensioned by wedges — a type of ceremonial drum well documented among the Senufo of Mali/Côte d'Ivoire. The form and iconography are consistent with Senufo carving traditions.

household.name: seat
household.title: seat
household.reason: The image shows a carved wooden zoomorphic (horse-head) stool/seat, a well-known Senufo furniture form used by diviners and elders. This matches the claimed Senufo household use.

household.name: loom-pulley; loom
household.title: loom-pulley; loom (?)
household.reason: Carved wooden loom-pulley with an antelope-head finial, a classic Senufo heddle-pulley used on narrow-strip looms in weaving; the museum directly attributes it to the Senufo, consistent with the claim.

household.name: pot
household.title: pot
household.reason: This is a carved wooden lidded vessel with a bird finial and geometric incised decoration, attributed by the museum to the Senufo — a plausible and characteristic piece of Senufo carving (the bird motif recalls Senufo hornbill imagery).

household.name: vävstol, ram
household.title: vävstol, ram
household.reason: This is a carved wooden pulley/heddle frame for a loom ("ram till vävtrissa för vävstol"), a bird-form heddle pulley of a type well documented among the Senufo of Côte d'Ivoire/Mali/Burkina Faso, cited with Goldwater's reference work on Senufo sculpture. Such carved loom pulleys are a characteristic Senufo craft object.

household.name: lås till dörr, Dörrlås
household.title: lås till dörr, Dörrlås
household.reason: This is a carved wooden door lock with a rider figure finial and metal key tappets, a well-documented Senufo/Ivory Coast object type used to secure doors — a genuine Senufo-made and -used item despite the "metalwork" mislabel (it is mainly carved wood with a small metal element).

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: This is a classic Senufo "mud cloth" (fini kodgi) with hand-spun cotton strips hand-sewn together and painted with stylized figures in mud dye and natural pigment — a well-documented Senufo textile tradition.

textile.name: textile
textile.title: textile
textile.reason: This is a classic Korhogo (fila/filafani) painted cloth from northern Côte d'Ivoire, decorated with stylized birds, animals and hunter/dancer figures in the traditional black-on-white mud-dye technique associated with Senufo hunters, dancers and initiates, exactly as described in the museum note.

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: A strip-woven cotton cloth with indigo, orange and grey pattern blocks, sewn from narrow handwoven strips as is typical of Senufo weaving traditions; museum records Senufo as maker.

garment.name: wrapper
garment.title: wrapper
garment.reason: Hand-woven strip cotton wrapper with indigo chequerboard bands and supplementary weft-float diamonds is a classic Senufo weaving type, well documented for this people of Mali/Côte d'Ivoire.

architectural.name: dörr
architectural.title: dörr
architectural.reason: The image is a detailed sketch of a carved wooden door from Ivory Coast attributed to the Senufo (Siena) people, decorated with a turtle, hornbill-like birds, a snake, cattle and figures in low relief — a well-documented Senufo architectural element (house/granary door).
